arc: Owner of the Stopped Pocket Watch
title: Episode 1: The Clock Stopped at 11:59

sentences.trans: It is 11:50 PM at night.
It is raining.
Seoyeon is a magazine editor.
Work finished late today.
But she does not have an umbrella.
In Seoyeon's bag, there is her grandmother's watch.
She went to a watch shop earlier today.
The old shop owner said,
"There is nothing broken.
However, it does not move.
The back does not open either."
Seoyeon runs into an alley.
It is an alley she walks past every day.

sentences.ko: 그런데 골목 끝에 작은 책방이 있어요.
sentences.ruby: 그런데|geureonde 골목|golmok 끝에|kkeute 작은|jageun 책방이|chaekbang-i 있어요.|isseoyo.
sentences.trans: However, at the end of the alley, there is a small bookstore.
It is a bookstore she has never seen before.
The name is 'Mulmangseolim'.
'Seolim' is an old word for 'bookstore'.
Jingle.
Seoyeon opens the door.
"Excuse me.
May I come inside for a moment?"

sentences.ko: 안경을 쓴 남자가 책을 읽고 있어요.
sentences.ruby: 안경을|angyeong-eul 쓴|sseun 남자가|namjaga 책을|chaegeul 읽고|ilkgo 있어요.|isseoyo.
sentences.trans: A man wearing glasses is reading a book.
The man closes the book and smiles.
"Yes, please come in.
It has been a while since I had a guest at this hour."
The man's name is Doyun.
He is the owner of this bookstore.
Doyun hands her a towel and warm citron tea.
"Thank you.
Are you open until late?"
"Yes.

sentences.ko: 저는 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요."
sentences.ruby: 저는|jeoneun 밤에|bame 잠을|jameul 잘|jal 못|mot 자요."|jayo."
sentences.trans: I don't sleep well at night."
Doyun's eyes look a bit tired.
Seoyeon opens her bag.
Just then, the watch drops to the floor.
Doyun picks up the watch.
The watch is stopped at 11:59.
"It is my grandmother's watch.
My grandmother passed away three months ago.

sentences.ko: 이 시계는 한 번도 안 움직였어요."
sentences.ruby: 이|i 시계는|sigyeneun 한|han 번도|beondo 안|an 움직였어요."|umjigyeosseoyo."
sentences.trans: This watch has never moved once."
Doyun hands the watch back.
"11:59... It is one minute before 12 o'clock."

sentences.ko: 땡, 땡, 땡… 책방의 큰 시계가 울려요.
sentences.ruby: 땡,|ttaeng, 땡,|ttaeng, 땡…|ttaeng... 책방의|chaekbang-ui 큰|keun 시계가|sigyega 울려요.|ullyeoyo.
sentences.trans: Dong, dong, dong... The large clock in the bookstore chimes.
It is 12 o'clock.
At that moment, the watch shines in Seoyeon's hand.
Tick, tock.
"Huh?
The watch is moving!"
Doyun touches the watch.
Another place appears before Doyun's eyes.
It is a rainy train station.
It is 'Gyeongseong Station'.
It is Seoul Station from 100 years ago.

sentences.ko: 한 여자가 이 시계를 들고 있어요.
sentences.ruby: 한|han 여자가|yeojaga 이|i 시계를|sigyereul 들고|deulgo 있어요.|isseoyo.
sentences.trans: A woman is holding this watch.
She is waiting for someone.
The woman's face cannot be seen.
Yet Doyun knows that woman.
She is a woman he has seen often in his dreams.
Doyun opens his eyes.
His face is pale.
Seoyeon looks at Doyun.
He is a person she is meeting for the first time.
Yet it feels like it is not the first time.
"Excuse me... Have we met somewhere before?"
Doyun cannot say anything.
Just then, click.
The back of the watch opens.
There are small letters inside.
"Let us meet again at midnight.

roleplay.situation: You enter a quiet bookstore late at night to escape the sudden rain.

quiz.question: Why did Seoyeon go into the bookstore?
options: She wanted to buy a new book.
It was raining and she did not have an umbrella.
She wanted to fix her watch.
quiz.explanation: Seoyeon stepped into the bookstore because it was raining late at night and she didn't have an umbrella.

quiz.question: What happens when the bookstore clock strikes 12?
options: The watch begins to shine and move.
quiz.explanation: At midnight (12 o'clock), the watch in Seoyeon's hand shines and its hands begin to tick.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for asking permission ('May I come in?').
quiz.explanation: '-아/어도 돼요?' expresses asking for permission ('들어가도 돼요?' = May I come in?).

sentences.ko: 마감을 끝내고 회사를 나왔을 때는 이미 밤 11시 50분이었다.

sentences.trans: Rain suddenly began pouring down, but Seoyeon didn't have an umbrella.
Seoyeon clutched her bag tightly.

sentences.ko: 그 안에는 할머니의 회중시계가 들어 있었다.

sentences.ko: 낮에 오래된 시계방에 갔을 때, 주인 할아버지는 고개를 저으며 말했다.
sentences.trans: When she visited an old watch repair shop earlier that day, the owner shook his head and spoke.

sentences.ko: "고장 난 곳은 없는데 이상하게 안 움직여요.
sentences.trans: "Nothing is broken, but strangely it won't run.

sentences.ko: 서연은 비를 피하려고 골목 안으로 뛰어 들어갔다.
sentences.trans: Seoyeon ran into an alley to shelter from the rain.

sentences.ko: 매일 지나다니던 골목인데, 끝에 처음 보는 책방 하나가 불을 밝히고 있었다.
sentences.trans: It was an alley she walked past every day, yet a unfamiliar bookstore at the end was glowing with light.
The sign read 'Mulmangseolim'.
It was an old-fashioned name meaning 'do not forget'.

sentences.ko: 딸랑, 문을 열자 작은 종이 울렸다.

sentences.trans: "Excuse me... may I stay inside just until the rain stops?"

sentences.ko: 책을 읽고 있던 남자가 책을 덮고 고개를 들었다.
sentences.trans: The man who had been reading closed his book and looked up.

sentences.ko: 베이지색 가디건에 은테 안경을 쓴 남자였다.
sentences.trans: He was a man wearing a beige cardigan and silver-rimmed glasses.
"Of course, please come in.

sentences.ko: 이 시간에 손님이 오신 건 오랜만이네요."
sentences.trans: It's been a long time since a guest arrived at this hour."

sentences.ko: 그는 자신을 책방 주인 한도윤이라고 소개했다.
sentences.trans: He introduced himself as Han Doyun, the owner of the bookstore.
Doyun handed her a towel and warm citron tea.
"Thank you.

"I have trouble sleeping at night.

sentences.ko: 어차피 깨어 있을 거라면 책방을 여는 게 낫더라고요."
sentences.trans: If I'm going to be awake anyway, I figured keeping the bookstore open was better."

sentences.ko: 그렇게 말하는 그의 눈은 조금 지쳐 보였다.
sentences.trans: As he said that, his eyes looked slightly exhausted.

sentences.ko: 수건을 꺼내려고 가방을 열다가 서연은 무언가를 바닥에 떨어뜨렸다.
sentences.trans: While opening her bag to pull out a towel, Seoyeon dropped something onto the floor.
Doyun bent down and picked it up.
It was an old pocket watch.
The hands were frozen at 11:59.
"It's a keepsake from my grandmother.

sentences.ko: 석 달 전에 돌아가셨는데, 제가 기억하는 동안 이 시계는 한 번도 움직인 적이 없어요."
sentences.trans: She passed away three months ago, and for as long as I can remember, this watch has never moved once."
Doyun said as he handed back the watch,
"11:59... exactly one minute before midnight."

sentences.ko: 바로 그때, 벽에 걸린 큰 시계가 자정을 알리기 시작했다.
sentences.trans: Right at that moment, the large wall clock began chiming midnight.

sentences.ko: 땡, 땡… 열두 번째 종소리가 울리자 서연의 손 위에서 회중시계가 희미하게 빛나기 시작했다.
sentences.trans: Dong, dong... As the twelfth bell chimed, the pocket watch in Seoyeon's hand began to glow faintly.

sentences.ko: 그리고 멈춰 있던 초침이 째깍째깍 움직였다.
sentences.trans: And the second hand, which had been still, began ticking.
"Unbelievable... the watch is moving!"

sentences.ko: 도윤이 조심스럽게 시계를 만지자, 그의 눈앞에 다른 풍경이 펼쳐졌다.
sentences.trans: When Doyun carefully touched the watch, a different scene unfolded before his eyes.
An old, rain-soaked train station.
The signboard read 'Gyeongseong Station'.
It was the name of Seoul Station 100 years ago.

sentences.ko: 그곳에서 한 여자가 이 시계를 꼭 쥔 채 누군가를 기다리고 있었다.
sentences.trans: There, a woman was tightly holding this watch while waiting for someone.

sentences.ko: 얼굴은 보이지 않았지만 도윤은 그 여자를 알았다.
sentences.trans: Her face couldn't be seen, but Doyun knew that woman.

sentences.ko: 잠들지 못하는 밤마다 꿈속에서 보던 바로 그 여자였다.
sentences.trans: She was the very woman he saw in his dreams every sleepless night.

sentences.ko: 환영에서 깨어난 도윤의 얼굴은 하얗게 질려 있었다.
sentences.trans: Waking from the vision, Doyun's face turned pale.

sentences.ko: 그런 도윤을 보는 순간, 서연은 가슴이 이상하게 두근거렸다.
sentences.trans: The moment Seoyeon looked at Doyun, her heart throbbed strangely.

sentences.ko: 이 장면을 어디선가 본 것 같았다.
sentences.trans: It felt like she had seen this scene somewhere before.

sentences.ko: "저기… 우리 전에 어디서 만난 적 있지 않아요?"
sentences.trans: "Excuse me... haven't we met somewhere before?"
Doyun couldn't answer at all.

sentences.ko: 그때 딸깍 소리와 함께, 절대 열리지 않던 뒤 뚜껑이 저절로 열렸다.
sentences.trans: Just then, with a click, the back cover that had never opened popped open on its own.

sentences.ko: 그 안에는 오래된 글씨가 새겨져 있었다.
sentences.trans: Inside, old writing was engraved.
"Let us meet again at midnight.

expressions.meaning: Used when an action occurs immediately after another ('as soon as...').

examples.trans: As soon as she opened the door, a small bell chimed.

expressions.meaning: Used to express an assumption based on observation ('it seems that...').

examples.trans: It seems you stay open until late.
It seems you are very tired.

roleplay.situation: You notice an old pocket watch dropped on your bookstore floor and return it to the guest.

quiz.question: What vision does Doyun experience when he touches the watch?
options: A modern editorial office in Seoul.
Gyeongseong Station 100 years ago with a woman waiting in the rain.
A clock repair shop in an alley.
quiz.explanation: Doyun sees Gyeongseong Station (Seoul Station 100 years ago) in the rain with a woman holding the pocket watch.

quiz.question: What is written inside the watch's back cover when it pops open?
quiz.explanation: The inscription inside reads '자정에 다시 만나요. 1925.' ('Let us meet again at midnight. 1925.').

quiz.question: What does the word '유품' mean in Korean?
quiz.explanation: '유품' refers to an item or keepsake left behind by someone who passed away.

quiz.question: Which grammar pattern expresses 'as soon as...' in '문을 열자 종이 울렸다'?
quiz.explanation: The connective ending '-자' indicates that the second action happens immediately upon the occurrence of the first action.

sentences.ko: 마감 원고를 넘기고 편집부를 나섰을 때, 시계는 이미 밤 11시 50분을 가리키고 있었다.

"Of course, please come in.

sentences.trans: It's been quite a while since a guest visited at this hour."

sentences.ko: 마치 손님을 맞는 시간이 따로 정해져 있다는 듯한 말투였다.

sentences.trans: As she cupped the teacup, warmth spread through her frozen fingertips.
"You seem to keep the shop open this late."
"Sleep doesn't come easily to me.

sentences.trans: Doyun bent down to pick it up.

Its rusted hands were fixed at 11:59.
"It's a heirloom from my grandmother.

"11:59... a time precisely one minute prior to midnight."

sentences.trans: Dong—dong—the moment the twelfth reverberation seeped into the air, Seoyeon gasped.

sentences.trans: Beneath the glass cover of the pocket watch resting on her palm, a subtle light bloomed, and the long-dormant second hand ticked back to life.

sentences.ko: 서연이 제 눈을 의심하는 사이, 도윤의 손끝이 시계에 닿았다.
sentences.trans: While Seoyeon doubted her own eyes, Doyun's fingertips brushed against the watch.

sentences.ko: 자욱한 증기와 기적 소리, 빗물에 잠긴 플랫폼.
sentences.trans: Dense steam, echoing train whistles, and a platform submerged in rain.

sentences.ko: 지금의 서울역이 백 년 전에 불리던 이름이었다.

sentences.trans: There, a woman clutching this very watch in both hands stood waiting for someone who would never arrive.
Her face remained obscured.
Yet Doyun knew who she was.

sentences.ko: 잠 못 드는 밤마다 꿈속에서 등을 돌린 채 서 있던, 바로 그 여인이었다.
sentences.trans: She was that very woman standing with her back turned in his dreams every sleepless night.

sentences.ko: 환영에서 빠져나온 도윤의 얼굴은 하얗게 질려 있었다.
sentences.trans: Emerging from the vision, Doyun's face was deathly pale.

sentences.ko: 그런 그를 마주한 순간, 서연의 가슴 깊은 곳에서 이름 붙일 수 없는 그리움이 밀물처럼 차올랐다.
sentences.trans: The moment she faced him, an indefinable longing swelled like a rising tide deep within Seoyeon's chest.

sentences.ko: 빗소리, 오래된 종이 냄새, 안경 너머의 저 눈빛까지.
sentences.trans: The sound of rain, the scent of aged paper, even that gaze behind his glasses.

sentences.ko: 언젠가 꼭 한 번 겪었던 장면 같았다.
sentences.trans: It felt like a scene she had experienced once before.
"Strange, isn't it?

sentences.ko: 처음 뵙는 분인데… 우리, 전에 어디서 만난 적 있지 않나요?"
sentences.trans: Even though this is our first meeting... haven't we met somewhere before?"
Doyun could not answer in the end.

sentences.ko: 대신 딸깍, 하는 작은 소리와 함께 꿈쩍도 않던 뒤 뚜껑이 저절로 열렸다.
sentences.trans: Instead, with a faint click, the back cover that hadn't budged popped open on its own.

sentences.ko: 닳아 희미해진 안쪽 면에는 단정한 필체가 새겨져 있었다.
sentences.trans: On the worn, faded inner surface, neat handwriting was engraved.
"Let us meet again at midnight.

편집부.exampleTrans: When she left the editorial department, it was raining.

붙박여.meaning: To be fixed / set firmly in place
붙박여.exampleTrans: The clock hands were fixed at 11:59.

밀물처럼.exampleTrans: Longing swelled up like a rising tide.

환영.exampleTrans: Doyun woke up from the vision.

expressions.meaning: Emphasizes that an event occurs immediately after another ('as soon as...', 'no sooner had... than...').

examples.trans: No sooner had he finished speaking than the grandfather clock chimed.
As soon as I arrived home, I fell asleep.

expressions.meaning: Used when stopping an ongoing action midway to do another ('stopping mid-action...').

examples.ko: 트렌치코트 깃을 여미다 말고 가방을 끌어안았다.
examples.trans: Midway through adjusting her coat collar, she stopped and hugged her bag.
He stopped eating midway and went outside.

roleplay.situation: You experience an inexplicable sense of familiarity upon seeing Doyun pale after touching the watch.
roleplay.ko: 처음 뵙는 분인데… 우리, 전에 어디서 만난 적 있지 않나요?
roleplay.pron: Cheoeum boemneun bun-inde... uri, jeone eodiseo mannan jeok itji annayo?

quiz.question: What literary detail highlights the eerie coincidence of the bookstore's name '勿忘書林'?
options: It is a chain bookstore recently opened in Seongsu-dong.
It means 'do not forget' and appears at a dead end Seoyeon passes daily.
It was named after Gyeongseong Station.
quiz.explanation: The name means 'Do Not Forget', an old bookshop standing unexpectedly at the end of a street Seoyeon frequently walks.

quiz.question: How does Doyun react after releasing his touch from the watch?
options: He laughs and hands it back calmly.
His face turns pale after experiencing a vivid historical vision.
He attempts to force open the back lid with tools.
He asks Seoyeon to sell him the watch.
quiz.explanation: Doyun emerges pale after seeing a vision of a woman holding the watch at rainy Gyeongseong Station 100 years ago.

quiz.question: What does '-기가 무섭게' mean in advanced Korean syntax?
options: Out of sudden fear of an event
Immediately as soon as an action finishes
quiz.explanation: '-기가 무섭게' expresses that the subsequent action occurs immediately upon completion of the prior action.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of '붙박이다' in '11시 59분에 붙박여 있었다'?
options: To be fixed or set firmly in place
quiz.explanation: '붙박이다' means to be fixed or firmly set in a specific position.
